title: Lymph node biopsy
also: fine needle aspiration of a lymph node
what: The doctor takes a piece of an enlarged lymph node, or removes the whole node, to look at it under a microscope. This is done with a needle and ultrasound, or through a small cut.
why: When a lymph node has been enlarged for a long time with no clear cause, for a possible blood disorder or tumor, or to clarify a diagnosis.
duration: a needle biopsy usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, removing a node 30 to 60 minutes; results usually in 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will decide if anything needs to change
Allergies, including to painkillers and numbing medicines

prepare.title: Type of biopsy
prepare.text: Your doctor will tell you whether a needle or a cut will be used, and what kind of numbing or anesthesia.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: With local numbing, you can usually eat. With general anesthesia, follow the clinic's rules on food and drink.

prepare.title: Someone with you
prepare.text: If you have anesthesia or sedation, you need someone to take you home.

bring: Your referral, tests, and lymph node ultrasound
Someone to take you home, if you have anesthesia
steps: You lie in a position that gives easy access to the node
The skin is cleaned and numbed
For a needle biopsy, the needle goes into the node with ultrasound guidance
For an open biopsy, a small cut is made and the node is removed
The spot is stitched or closed with skin tape
feel: A prick and stinging from the numbing
Afterward, mild pain and swelling at the spot
after: You usually go home the same day
Keep the bandage dry for as long as your doctor says
Stitches are removed after 7 to 10 days, or they dissolve
Your doctor usually explains the results at a visit
red_flags: Strong swelling, or blood soaking through the bandage
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus at the cut
If the biopsy was on the neck and it becomes hard to breathe or swallow: call emergency services

faq.q: Is an enlarged lymph node dangerous?
faq.a: Most often lymph nodes swell because of an infection. A biopsy is needed to find the exact cause.
Sometimes the whole node is needed for an accurate diagnosis, not just a piece. Your body works fine without one node.

reminders.text: Lymph node biopsy tomorrow. Check if you can eat in the morning. Bring your ultrasound and a list of medicines.
